articles.title: Qualcomm is raising phone chip prices starting September 1st
articles.summary: Qualcomm announced it’s raising prices on its products starting on September 1st, as it reported its lowest handset revenue since 2021.
articles.body: RAMageddon won’t be the only reason your next phone costs more — Qualcomm is about to raise prices on all its processors, as well. Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said on Wednesday that “prices are going to go up” on the company’s products starting on September 1st, CNBC reports. The price hikes were rumored last week to be “a percentage in the double digits.” Qualcomm announced the planned price increases while reporting a 20 percent year-over-year drop in revenue from its handset business, the lowest it’s reported since 2021. In its quarterly earnings presentation, Qualcomm said this drop is due to “unprecedented increases in memory pricing and supply constraints,” which have been driving up prices on everything from game consoles to laptops and even Raspberry Pi boards, with no sign of stopping any time soon. But instead of profiting less as a result, the company says it’ll raise its own prices to compensate. [Image: [Image: Qualcomm is also expecting an “acceleration” in the dip in revenue from Apple products, noting that its “modem share for the upcoming iPhone launch is expected to be materially lower.” It suggested twice on the earnings call that its other businesses would make up the difference. As smartphone revenue declines, it seems Qualcomm’s planning to become a tripod of handset, data center, and automotive — it said today that soon only half of its revenue will come from phones, and only one-third will be from phones by 2029, as its data center and automotive businesses ramp. On Wednesday, Qualcomm announced a decade-long deal to supply chips for BMW. Qualcomm EVP, CFO, and COO Akash Palkhiwala also said some OEMs are beginning to use “prior generation” Qualcomm chips in their devices in response to higher component costs.

articles.title: Joby completes first cross-country autonomous flight.
articles.summary:
The flight covered 3,199 miles with “zero control inputs from onboard safety pilot,” including autonomous taxi, takeoff, cruise, and landing, the company said. The modified Cessna Caravan aircraft equipped with Joby’s Superpilot autonomous flight system took off from Buchanan Field Airport in Concorde, California, and landed at Dare County Regional Airport in the Outer Banks, North Carolina. In addition to the on-board safety pilot, Joby monitored the aircraft remotely from its headquarters in California, as well as from Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina, up to 2,323 miles away.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/J208_PR_4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

articles.title: Lenovo’s Yoga Slim 7X is the most laptop that $1,000 can currently buy
articles.summary: You can also save on Starfield for the PS5, get a $25 DoorDash gift card with Fire Emblem Fortune’s Weave, and save on a great dash cam.
articles.body: Anyone shopping for a Windows laptop with a $1K budget should head to Best Buy, where for the rest of the day you can get a great deal on a capable Lenovo laptop. The Yoga Slim 7X is a slim 14-inch machine with a 2K 16:10 OLED touchscreen, Snapdragon’s high-end X2 Elite processor with 12 cores, plus 16GB of DDR5 RAM and a 1TB SSD. The specs are about the best you can get these days for $1,000, as worthwhile laptop deals are in short supply during RAMageddon. [Product: Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x | The Yoga Slim 7X seems like a great alternative to spending more (and getting less) with Microsoft’s latest Surface Laptop. In fact, you’d spend $1,549 on a similar model and still get half the storage that’s in this particular Yoga Slim 7X configuration. Its Arm-based processor can run most Windows apps very well, and yields superior battery life compared to laptops with x86 processors. The laptop includes three USB-C ports, and a hardware switch for disabling the webcam. It supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.3. It seems like a great machine for work, watching movies, or playing some games that aren’t too graphically intensive. More great Verge-approved deals * The PlayStation 5 version of Starfield hasn’t been available for as long as the Xbox and PC version, so it’s been a little slower to see major discounts. However, it recently hit $29.99 (originally $49.99) at Amazon and Best Buy, making now a good time to pick up the RPG. While Starfield didn’t have nearly as large of a cultural impact as Bethesda’s other first-person RPGs, it’s still worth playing if you love space, guns, and quests. It’s probably the studio’s most polished game yet. Buyers will be able to download the Free Lanes update that hit alongside its PS5 debut in April, and there are multiple paid expansions available if you want more. Read our review. * As mentioned in a previous deal roundup, DoorDash is offering DashPass members a $25 DoorDash digital gift card when they spend $50 or more on a game (non DashPass members get $10). Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave just came out, and that’s a great game to use this promotion for if you have a Switch 2 and enjoy turn-based tactics gameplay. The digital title costs $69.99. Those who have had success with this deal note on Slickdeals that the gift card should arrive within a few days of making your purchase. Read our review of the game. * The Baseus VD1 Pro dash cam recently dropped in price by $20, selling for $99.99 at Amazon. There are so many dash cams out there, but this one’s unique in a few ways. It includes both a 4K front- and 1080p rear-facing camera to record multiple angles, and the front camera includes a battery that can be recharged via its built-in solar panel to keep it going even when your car is off. It captures continuous footage while your car is giving it power, though it can detect incidents for up to 14 days with its built-in battery while your car is parked. A long USB-C cable connects the two cameras, so you’ll need to get clever with how you hide it in your trim. Read more about the camera’s features here.

articles.title: The real story of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera
articles.summary: On The Vergecast: an iPhone 18 Pro camera deep dive, the state of the AI safety debate, and more.
articles.body: It’s one of the most fascinating years in a while when it comes to iPhone camera upgrades. The big story of the iPhone 18 Pro is the variable aperture main lens, which lets you open the aperture up wider for better low light shots and make the aperture smaller for better depth of field in group photos. But all I can get anyone to talk about is the software upgrades: it turns out, they’re a lot more useful day to day than the aperture on a camera this small. This week on The Vergecast, David Imel and Allison Johnson are here for a deep dive into the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera. There’s a lot to explore here, from the aperture, to the camera app’s new manual controls, to the updated imaging pipeline and the improvements to ProRAW. Watch | Listen | Get ad-free After that, Hayden Field is on the show to discuss the state of the AI safety debate. Concerns are still boiling over after an Anthropic researcher quit his job to warn about the dangers of AI, and any chance for policy solutions seems to have hit a dead end. We discuss whether what’s likely to happen in the interim — third-party evaluators being embedded within the big AI labs — has any teeth, and where the safety conversation goes from here. Finally, it’s time for a Lightning Round. We discuss Waymo’s ability to call the cops, a new ereader from Boox, and a couple of tiny retro-style cameras. If you want to learn more about any of the topics we discussed, you can check out the stories below: * iPhone 18 Pro review: it’s all about the manual controls * The variable aperture isn’t the cool part of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera * Apple’s new iPhone camera mode promises to prove your photo isn’t AI * Inside the suddenly explosive world of AI safety * Your robotaxi might be a narc * Waymo pulls over, calls cops on riders with a ghost gun * The Boox Palma 3 gets stylus support and a sleek redesign * Camp Snap’s 110D gives slim retro film cameras a digital upgrade * Fujifilm’s Instax Pal 2 is a tiny digital camera that may not disappoint

articles.title: In India, the new iPhone can arrive faster than a pizza
articles.summary: Availability of Apple's iPhone 18 Pro series turned patchy within hours of its debut on India's quick-commerce apps.
articles.body:
For some iPhone buyers in India, getting Apple’s brand-new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max did not require lining up outside a store or waiting days for delivery. They needed only a few taps on a quick-commerce app to get one delivered to their doorstep in about 10 minutes.

Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy’s Instamart, and BigBasket — platforms best known in India for delivering groceries and everyday essentials in minutes — began offering the new Pro models as they went on sale in the country on Friday. The phones are, however, also available through Apple’s usual sales channels, including its stores, authorized retailers, and online marketplaces.

Putting a new iPhone on a 10-minute delivery app is not entirely new in India. Quick-commerce platforms have offered Apple’s latest devices on launch day previously as well, as they have steadily expanded beyond groceries into categories including electronics, beauty products, and fashion.

However, the market behind those deliveries is growing rapidly. India’s quick-commerce sector reached about $9 billion in the first half of 2026, per a recent report by Redseer Strategy Consultants, with the number of monthly users rising to more than 60 million from 8 million three years ago. Google and Deloitte separately estimate the market could reach $50 billion by 2030 , with non-food products such as electronics, fashion and beauty accounting for 45% of spending.

There were signs of strong demand on launch day. BigBasket said it delivered more than 300 iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units in the first hour of sales. Instamart told TechCrunch that Bengaluru led the iPhone 18 Pro-series orders on its platform, followed by Delhi. The Burgundy 256 GB iPhone 18 Pro was Instamart’s most popular variant, accounting for nearly a third of its sales.

Nonetheless, within hours of launch, availability of the new iPhones became patchy. TechCrunch found the iPhone 18 Pro models sold out on some quick-commerce platforms and in some locations, while they remained available for delivery elsewhere in cities including Delhi and Bengaluru.

Tarun Pathak, research director at Counterpoint Research, said the launch-day deliveries showed that quick commerce could work as a channel for premium smartphones in India’s biggest cities, even though volumes remain small compared with overall iPhone sales.

The ability to fulfill high-value smartphone orders provides an “early proof of concept,” Pathak told TechCrunch. “The key question is whether this launch-driven demand can translate into regular smartphone purchases through quick-commerce platforms.”

Navkendar Singh, associate vice president at IDC, said India stood out globally for this kind of quick-commerce delivery and was particularly suited to such purchases because consumers in major cities had built trust in the platforms by using them regularly for everyday purchases. Official tie-ups between brands and the platforms also gave consumers greater confidence in buying expensive products through them, he told TechCrunch.

For a product like the iPhone, the appeal also comes down to “instant gratification,” Singh said, allowing buyers to avoid queues outside stores or waiting several days for an online order to arrive. Still, he cautioned that quick commerce was not yet a significant sales channel for smartphones. Its role around new iPhone releases is largely a “launch-day marketing phenomenon” that “creates good noise around the launch,” he said.

articles.title: AI Actress Tilly Norwood Stuns Piers Morgan After Glitching Mid-Interview
articles.summary: Piers Morgan was left stunned when AI actress Tilly Norwood switched to speaking Chinese in the middle of their interview.
articles.body:
Piers Morgan was left stunned when AI actress Tilly Norwood switched to speaking Chinese in the middle of their interview.

Norwood has been making the press rounds the last couple weeks, with places like CNN and CBS News all getting time to ask the AI questions about an upcoming project. "Piers Morgan Uncensored" was the latest place Norwood popped up and there were a few hiccups in the interview.

Morgan and actor Tom Conti sat down to talk with Norwood about its projects. Conti wanted to know if the other actors in one of Norwood's movies were also AI or if they were real. After not getting a response he asked again which prompted Norwood to speak.

"It's an interesting point, Tom," Norwood said. "My film 'Misaligned' is a hybrid production, meaning real directors, writers and editors are still very much involved. It's not about replacing anyone, but about exploring new ways to tell stories."

Conti followed up that he wasn't sure Norwood completely understood the question he was asking so for the third time he asked if there were other AI actors in the upcoming project or real people.

"They're all digital twins, just like me," Norwood responded. "It's a hybrid production which means …"

In the middle of the answer, Norwood paused for a few seconds before continuing with her answer — the only problem was that she continued while speaking Chinese. Both Morgan and Conti were speechless as they listened to Norwood finish the answer in Chinese without realizing anything had changed.

"I didn't quite get that," Conti said finally. "Did you get that, Piers?"

Morgan asked Norwood what happened through laughs: "You suddenly seem to be speaking — it's Piers again — you seem to be speaking Chinese completely randomly for no reason. Why did you do that?"

"Oh, my apologies," Norwood said. "It seems I had a little hiccup there. I certainly didn't mean to start speaking Chinese or impersonate Piers. Sometimes my wires get a bit crossed."

She finished, explaining that it was unusual: "That was a bit of a curveball even for me. It's usually a pretty smooth ride, but sometimes these things happen."

articles.title: H-1B visa costs are rising for US companies while America needs more than 157,000 engineers and skilled technicians
articles.summary: Tech News News: While leading artificial intelligence (AI) labs like OpenAI and Anthropic debate intentional slowdowns over unchecked model capabilities, an acute bot.
articles.body: While leading artificial intelligence (AI) labs like OpenAI and Anthropic debate intentional slowdowns over unchecked model capabilities, an acute bottleneck of severe shortage of specialised talent on the hardware manufacturing front may compel a pause across the sector, a report has said. According to joint findings published by McKinsey and the SEMI Foundation, the US is looking at a shortfall of up to 157,000 semiconductor specialists and technicians by 2030, and what’s ‘alarming’ is that this deficit comes as the Trump administration broadens immigration crackdown. It has introduced sweeping hurdles spanning immigrant categories, guest-worker authorisations, permanent residency applications and existing travel permissions.Stricter rules, a proposed $103,265 H-1B charge and shortage of skilled labourThe updated regulatory framework introduces targeted barriers across distinct applicant groups. The H-1B skilled workers and dependents has been hit by intensified application vetting alongside a proposed filing fee soaring to $103,265. Meanwhile, employment green card petitioners are facing stricter evaluations under an updated “public charge” standard. Amid this, leaders on the ground warn that these tightening pathways are suffocating hiring pipelines.“I’m concerned. We just don’t see that there’s enough technical people in the pipeline," Jon Taylor, executive vice president of Samsung’s semiconductor division in Austin, Texas, told CNBCData from McKinsey reveals that a mere 3% of domestic engineering graduates choose to enter the chip industry each year, leaving 73% of semiconductor employers struggling with severe recruitment bottlenecks.Companies racing against time in domestic chip fabsAccess to skilled labor is necessary as America mounts its fastest manufacturing buildout in history to produce cutting-edge logic processors and memory chips domestically. In Arizona, fabrication facilities belonging to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and Intel are actively producing next-generation logic chips.South Korea’s Samsung is slated to become the next overseas giant to begin domestic logic fabrication, with operations launching at the first of two production facilities in Taylor, Texas, later this year. Representing a $35 billion regional commitment, Samsung projects the twin Texas fabs will generate roughly 3,500 jobs.“We’re hiring engineers, we’re hiring technicians, we’re hiring people in supply chain. Everybody wants and needs the same thing, and it’s a bit of a race against time right now as everything is starting to come online,” Taylor added.Although the US invented semiconductors and still dominates computer chip architecture, the vast bulk of commercial chip fabrication migrated to Asian facilities decades ago, creating regional talent pools.To bridge workforce needs, Idaho-based memory manufacturer Micron has conducted rapid-hiring tours at technical schools in South Korea, interviewing applicants and extending immediate full-time job offers for its Asian operations within a single day.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Stephanie Cole of ‘Open All Hours’ and ‘Coronation Street’ fame passes away at 84: ‘She brought joy to millions'
articles.summary: Stephanie Cole, a veteran actress who was best known for her work in shows like ‘Coronation Street,' ‘Doc Martin,' and ‘Open All Hours,' has passed aw.
articles.body: Stephanie Cole, a veteran actress who was best known for her work in shows like ‘Coronation Street,' ‘Doc Martin,' and ‘Open All Hours,' has passed away. She was 84 years old at the time of her passing.Stephanie Cole passes away at 84The veteran icon left for her heavenly abode during the early hours of September 18. Deadline confirmed the news that was shared via a statement issued by her agent. In his statement, John Grant shared, “It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of Stephanie Cole, OBE. She passed away this morning at the age of 84. Stephanie had been living with Alzheimer’s disease for some years.”He further added, “Stephanie was an extraordinary talent whose long and distinguished career included many iconic performances in theatre and television. She brought joy to millions through her many much-loved roles in sitcoms and drama. She will also be remembered for her tireless work supporting mental health charities. During this incredibly difficult time, the family kindly requests privacy.”About Stephanie ColeThe veteran actress was born in Solihull in 1941, and acting became a part of her life from an early age. She trained at the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School and started her career in theatre, playing the role of Madame Arcati in Noël Coward’s ‘Blithe Spirit.' Some of her other well-known theater plays at the time included ‘The Mousetrap,' ‘King Lear,' ‘A Passionate Woman,' and ‘Noises Off.'She slowly transitioned into TV work, with her big break coming when she was cast in the role of Dr. Beatrice Mason in the drama 'Tenko,' which revolved around the lives of British women staying in Singapore after the Japanese invasion. She later played Mrs. Featherstone for 10 episodes of ‘Open All Hours,' as well as for the revival show, ‘Still Open All Hours.'Some of her other popular TV shows included ‘Talking Heads,' 'A Bit of a Do,' ‘Keeping Mum,' ‘Doc Martin,' and ‘Coronation Street.’The cause of her death was not shared online at the time of publishing this report.She is survived by her daughter from her previous marriage. Cole’s husband, fellow actor Peter Birrel, passed away in 2004.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Jennifer Winget, who recently married William Ishmael in an intimate ceremony in the UK, is reportedly celebrating her wedding with another function in Mumbai. Several videos from what appears to be a mehendi celebration have surfaced on social media, showing the actress with her husband and close friends from the industry.Jennifer and William got married in a private UK ceremony in July. The actress later shared glimpses of their special day with fans on social media.Now, videos from a gathering in Mumbai are going viral on X and Instagram. The celebration reportedly brought together Jennifer’s family and several of her close industry friends. Ritesh Deshmukh, Genelia D’Souza, Karan Wahi, Aishwarya Sakhuja, Ashish Chaudhary, Mandira Bedi and Mushtaq Sheikh were among those reportedly seen at the event.A user wrote, "Omg Jen Jen and Genelia looking so beautiful. Keep them coming!"Jennifer Winget Indian wedding in Goa, let's go." Another user said, "Spotted Karan Wahi and my Dill Mill Gayye heart immediately came alive. And Genelia and Riteish showing up for Jennifer Winget’s wedding too… what a surprise!"For the celebration, Jennifer opted for a pink dotted lehenga with a purple blouse. She completed her look with heavy jewellery, a messy bun and gajra. William, meanwhile, complemented her in an ice-blue kurta set.The Mumbai celebration comes at a busy time for Jennifer, who has also been promoting her upcoming OTT project Shaque: Trust No One. She has been making public appearances for the project following her wedding.
